title: Flow-control tokens and stall recovery for partial streaming generations
creator: Alicia Park
description:
Problem: Clients that disconnect mid-generation or that are slow to read streaming deltas create two classes of server-side resource pressure: (1) unbounded KV/prefix retention for partially-emitted generations and (2) head-of-line blocking of batched GPU work because the server preserves in-flight state waiting for slow/paused clients. Both increase tail latency and cost and can cause capacity churn on Dedicated pools.

Goal: Implement a cooperative flow-control scheme that combines short-lived client-issued tokens (client-holdoff tokens) with server-side stall detection and a safety-net partial-generation compaction process. This should allow the runtime to reclaim memory and GPU slot reservations predictably, reduce head-of-line stalls, and provide safe resumability or graceful trimming of partially-generated outputs for disconnected clients.

High-level approach: Issue a lightweight per-stream flow-control token when a stream is established. Tokens encode a small lease TTL and an explicit backlog window (max pending deltas before backpressure). Clients must refresh tokens periodically while actively consuming. Server enforces two limits: an aggressive in-memory reservation TTL and a longer reconciliation window during which we keep compacted prefixes to allow resume or post-hoc retrieval. A background compaction pass will convert evacuated partial generations into compacted prefix blobs and free GPU KV resources.

Why this differs from existing work: Existing tickets focused on lease-based ownership and adaptive backpressure (ENG-44610) or incremental TTL pruning for partial outputs (ENG-101234). This effort ties client-driven refresh semantics to a server-side stall detector and explicit compaction handoff, avoiding long-lived opaque leases and enabling measurable metrics for client misbehavior and slow-consumer detection.
acceptance_criteria: Clients receive a flow-control token at stream start and can refresh it via a light-weight keepalive call
Server enforces backlog window: new generations for a client are paused when backlog exceeds configured threshold
Compaction background job converts partial generations older than reservation_ttl into compacted prefix blobs and frees GPU KV memory
Disconnected clients can either resume within reconciliation_window or request trimmed result with a stable placeholder error code
Unit + integration tests cover token refresh, stall detection, compaction correctness, and race conditions with KV cache eviction
Performance: median tail-tail latency for unrelated concurrent streams should not regress by more than 5% under synthetic slow-consumer load
Metric coverage: per-stream token_refresh_rate, stream_stall_count, compaction_rate, reclaimed_kv_bytes, resume_success_rate
implementation_plan: Design flow-control token format and minimal API: token_lease_ttl (ms), backlog_window (deltas), token_refresh endpoint
Add server-side stall detector: per-stream sliding-window read progress + backlog count; emit stream_stall_count metric
Implement in-memory reservation TTL and background compaction job that writes compacted prefixes to blobstore and frees KV cache entries
Add client SDK helpers (JS/Python) to honor tokens and refresh proactively; implement graceful fallback for legacy clients without token support
Create migration/compatibility layer: if no token seen, apply stricter short reservation TTL and a fast-compaction path to avoid resource starvation
End-to-end tests with simulated slow readers, abrupt disconnects, and reconnection scenarios; run on dedicated-reserved capacity to validate resource reclamation
Rollout: feature-flag behind runtime-1.20 gate; start with internal-only traffic, promote to canary customers, then global rollout with telemetry and SLA watch
testing_plan: Unit tests for token issuance, refresh, and expiry handling
Integration: simulate N clients with configurable consumer speeds and measure reclaimed_kv_bytes over time
Chaos tests: abrupt client disconnects during compaction and resume attempts post-compaction
Load test on Dedicated: validate no regressions in throughput when 10% of connections are slow-consumers
Compatibility tests: ensure legacy SDKs without token refresh are subject to fast-compaction policy but still receive deterministic errors
metrics_and_alerts: stream_stall_count: counter (alert if increase > 3x baseline in 5m)
token_refresh_rate: gauge (alert if drops below 90% of expected for internal clients)
compaction_rate: gauge (track how many partial generations compacted per minute)
reclaimed_kv_bytes: gauge (critical to validate memory savings)
resume_success_rate: ratio over 5m (alert if < 95% during canary)
SLO_impact: track 99th percentile latency for unrelated streams during canary
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Aggressive compaction may trim user-visible outputs unexpectedly. Mitigation: two-window approach (reservation_ttl + reconciliation_window) and explicit placeholder error codes informing clients about trimming with clear retry semantics.

Risk: Legacy clients that never refresh tokens may be repeatedly compacted. Mitigation: compatibility path with short TTL and opt-in extended retention via header/feature flag; notify customers via Console if their traffic is affected.

Risk: Background compaction load spikes may impact GPU scheduling. Mitigation: run compaction on dedicated control-plane workers with rate limiting and off-peak scheduling, and throttle compaction when node load is high.

Risk: Race between compaction and resume. Mitigation: atomic handoff: write compacted blob and then free KV entries only after blobstore commit is confirmed; resume returns compacted retrieval endpoint with metadata
dependencies_notes: Depends on ENG-44610 for adaptive backlog heuristics and eviction policy primitives
Coordination with storage team to ensure compacted prefix blobs are addressable and low-latency for resume paths
SDK and docs work: update streaming API spec and examples for token refresh semantics
